seoTitle: Set Up ATM-Style Trade Management in TradingView
metaDescription: See how to preset stop loss and take profit levels in TradingView using bracket orders, similar to NinjaTrader's Advanced Trade Management system.
intro: TradingView doesn't have a native ATM strategy feature like NinjaTrader, but you can recreate the effect using bracket orders through connected brokers. This guide explains how to preset your stop loss and take profit before confirming a trade, so you get faster, more consistent risk management.

steps.heading: Understand the workaround
steps.body: TradingView lacks a built-in ATM feature, but supported brokers such as Binance, OANDA, or TradeStation let you configure bracket-style orders through the Trading Panel.

steps.heading: Enable bracket orders in your broker
steps.body: Check your connected broker's settings for bracket order support, which lets stop loss and take profit attach automatically to a new trade.

steps.heading: Set your default risk-to-reward ratio
steps.body: Configure a preferred risk-to-reward ratio so your SL and TP levels are calculated consistently across trades.

steps.heading: Adjust SL/TP by ticks, pips, or percentage
steps.body: Choose the measurement that fits your instrument and set your stop loss and target distance accordingly.

steps.heading: Modify orders after execution
steps.body: Once a trade is live, you can quickly adjust the SL or TP directly on the chart if market conditions change.

steps.heading: Consider Pine Script alerts for automation
steps.body: For more customized entry and exit logic, Pine Script alerts can help automate parts of your setup beyond manual bracket orders.

faq.question: Does TradingView have a built-in ATM strategy feature?
faq.answer: No, TradingView doesn't have a native ATM feature like NinjaTrader, but bracket orders through supported brokers achieve a similar result.

faq.question: Which brokers support bracket orders on TradingView?
faq.answer: Brokers such as Binance, OANDA, and TradeStation can support preset stop loss and take profit levels when connected to TradingView.

faq.question: Can I set a default risk-to-reward ratio?
faq.answer: Yes, you can configure a default ratio so your SL and TP levels are applied consistently to new trades.

faq.question: Does this work on mobile?
faq.answer: Bracket order support and mobile compatibility can vary by broker, so it's worth checking your broker's mobile capabilities.

faq.question: Can I automate entries and exits further?
faq.answer: Yes, Pine Script alerts can be used to build more customized automated entry and exit logic.
